scope: Read-only source review. Mechanisms below are not measured timing costs or causal attribution of any benchmark delta.
disabled_definition: Clear all FC_POOL_* variables. Merely omitting the PoolCache action or admitting zero pages does not disable observation when drive identity opt-in remains configured.

findings.finding: DiskProperties::new calls disk_identity once per constructed/restored drive. For a read-only drive with FC_POOL_IMAGE_PATH absent it performs that environment lookup and returns None. Writable drives short-circuit before the lookup. There is no identity cloning/index allocation here when None.

PendingRequest now carries an Option<(String,u64,u64)> initialized to None. For reads process checks disk.pool_identity; None means the map closure does not execute, hence no ID clone and no environment lookup or pool mutex on this path. Complete successful reads additionally test the pending Option; None skips observe. The enlarged request state and option/branch operations remain, so zero overhead cannot be asserted. Exact generated instruction/layout costs have not been measured.

findings.topic: Enabled hints even without mapped sharing
findings.finding: A configured read-only identity causes one String clone into every read request, including reads that later fail or are unaligned. On complete successful aligned reads, observe locks a process-local Mutex and inserts one BTreeMap entry per full 4KiB page, cloning the image ID for each entry. New entries may allocate tree nodes; replacements drop the prior owned Hint. This is the mechanism of the observation-enabled arm, not the fully disabled arm.

findings.topic: Lifecycle work remains when pooling is disabled
findings.finding: resume_vm and save_state call mapping_failed(), which initializes/checks OnceLock and locks the pool Mutex even with all opt-in variables absent. First initialization checks FC_POOL_HINTS_RESTORE once and otherwise constructs an empty state. save_state also calls dump_hints; with FC_POOL_HINTS unset it returns after an environment lookup without acquiring its own lock or serializing/writing hints. create_snapshot calls has_overlays only when dax_offset is Some because of short-circuit evaluation; an ordinary non-DAX snapshot skips that lock.

The hint hook is reached through queued virtio-blk requests. A guest file-cache hit that issues no virtio-blk read executes no observer callback, Bloom lookup or hint-index operation. This does not imply equal end-to-end hit latency: backing placement, page faults, CoW, and other system effects must be measured separately.

findings.topic: Scope of pristine versus patched-disabled timing
findings.finding: The final patched executable includes earlier DAX/handoff/storage changes in addition to the pool module. An end-to-end stock versus patched-disabled delta measures their aggregate effect plus run variation. The above gates identify possible work but cannot establish which mechanism caused a measured delta.

Stock File snapshot restore opens the RAM file and maps it MAP_PRIVATE with read/write protections. Multiple processes on the same host mapping the same underlying regular-file inode and offset can initially refer to the same host page-cache folio; later writes become private CoW. Thus stock snapshot clones can already physically share untouched guest RAM, including previously warmed guest file-cache data, without this pooling implementation or KSM. Sharing is conditional and must be verified after guest resume; the source does not guarantee every page stays shared.

findings.topic: What stock snapshot sharing does not imply
findings.finding: Independent cold boots use separate anonymous guest-memory mappings for ordinary virtio-blk. Sharing an image file in the host page cache is not the same as sharing the guest destination frames: the sync block engine reads into each guest memory slice. Separate RAM-snapshot file inodes do not gain the same-file page-cache identity merely because their bytes or disk extents match. Ordinary NFS mappings on different hosts likewise have separate host kernel page caches; same-file clone sharing on one host is not proof of cross-host shared physical CXL pages.

findings.topic: Stock on CXL exposed as ordinary NUMA System RAM
findings.finding: Conditional inference from the allocation paths and Linux policy: if CXL capacity is onlined as normal System RAM, unmodified Firecracker anonymous guest-memory allocations can use that memory according to host NUMA/cpuset policy. Stock does not need this explicit devDAX patch merely to run on pages physically located in CXL. The Linux dax/kmem driver adds System RAM, and a parent-established NUMA task policy survives exec. This has not been validated by the current devDAX experiment and is not the same as cross-host pooling or handoff.

findings.topic: What explicit devDAX support adds here
findings.finding: The patch recognizes FC_DAX_RAM/FC_DAX_OFFSET and directly maps a chosen character-device range MAP_SHARED as guest RAM, validating device alignment/capacity. Its restore path reuses that selected range. Pool admission separately remaps validated 4KiB payload pages MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_FIXED to frozen canonical devDAX offsets with the lab kernel CoW support. These are explicit backing/address/lifecycle mechanisms, not ordinary NUMA placement.

comparison_reporting_constraints: Label independently booted stock VMs and same-snapshot stock clones as distinct baselines.
Report both guest page-cache residency and actual payload PFN sharing; a VMA or same image path alone is insufficient.
Distinguish fully disabled observation from enabled hints with admission disabled.
Do not describe ordinary Firecracker as categorically unable to use CXL System RAM.
Do not attribute benchmark deltas to locks, String allocation, NUMA latency, or KVM behavior without supporting measurements.
